note: The OLG covers fleeing felon ineligibility on the 'SNAP Disqualifications and Sanctions' page (section: Disqualification of Fleeing Felons, updated April 2025). It describes the alternative/Martinez test: law enforcement must present a felony arrest warrant with NCIC codes 4901 (Escape), 4902 (Flight to Avoid), or 4999 (Flight-Escape) and inform the state agency of intent to apprehend. This aligns with one of the two FNS-specified methods. However, the OLG does not mention the four-part test described in FNS 848.1 (outstanding felony warrant + individual awareness + evasive action + law enforcement actively seeking). FNS requires that the State Plan specify which test the state has adopted, so Massachusetts may have intentionally adopted only the Martinez test — but this is an inference, as the State Plan is not available to confirm. The BEACON 'Limitations on Program Eligibility' pages collect self-reported fleeing felon information via Q&A but do not describe either verification test. The OLG also does not mention the State Plan requirement itself. Finding: OLG adequately covers the Martinez/alternative test but omits the four-part test entirely — whether this is a gap or an intentional state policy choice cannot be confirmed without the State Plan.
